steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, I would like an explanation.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I knew things weren't as simple as they seemed...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Inquisition is simply keeping too many more secrets than the Iberian people deserve to know.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: My lady, need I remind you that spreading rumors and hearsay is strictly forbidden in Iberia?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: High Inquisitor, I'm only saying this because you already know those secrets.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Church of the Deep has infiltrated Iberia and is taking root here in secret.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They took advantage of the relationship you once had with the sea. Abandoned Iberian cities have become the beachhead for the Church of the Deep's encroachment onto dry land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They have their own interpretations of your scriptures, and they use them to bend your will. They also hide well. With so many irons in the fire, there was never any way for you to attend to all of it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So... you should cry out for help. If you continue this pointless war of territory and faith, we will miss our one chance.

a.text: The Hunters and the Inquisitor find themselves in a peculiar face off with Kal'tsit. Skadi starts to think that perhaps Kal'tsit is actually on her side.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your Honor, Iberians are different.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The skyline that you see every day is different from what everyone else who walks this world sees.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What do you call the place where you live every day and night? The coast.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Other peoples live on land, while Iberians live by the coast.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: For the majority of the population, whether they live in the wilderness or the cities, their sightlines are the sky above and an endless swath of land and mountains ahead.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Anything above the clouds means nothing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When they talk about 'the world', they refer to these lands alone.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The land on which they live is the world to them, because they've decided there is nothing in this world beyond these lands.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Whether residing in sealed-off cities, out-of-the-way villages, or hostile wilderness, they believe in what they see, and nothing else.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now look at them again. These Abyssal Hunters. These Ægir.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The ocean is vast in ways beyond the land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Iberia is not like other countries.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Those who reside on land are obsessed with their ways and their authorities. They overlook the infinite possibilities, and the opportunities to explore the boundaries that they blindly choose to ignore.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your world is far more complete. You understand both the land and the sea. Iberia has a much better knowledge of its place in the world than anyone else.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This has given you a huge lead over everyone in the past.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: That is enough.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: This is all water under the bridge. The radiance of the cities has faded, and Iberia is nothing but a pile of rubble today.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What a surprise. I thought you would dodge the subject.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: You are here, and you are certainly not blind. Look out and see for yourself.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Cities like Sal Viento line the entire Iberian coastline.
Iberia was once a prosperous nation, but how many of these ruins can be found here today?
Kal'tsit knows, and naturally the High Inquisitor knows too. However, with the High Inquisitor's steely composure, it is impossible to discern any kind of emotion from his expression whatsoever.
Furthermore, he is wearing a mask.
If they could cry, then the Iberians would definitely cry. If they could laugh, then the Iberians would definitely laugh out loud.
Yet here stands one such impassioned Iberian, who has since turned into the emotionless man before her.
Without expression and without emotion. Iberia's golden age has passed into a life of tranquility.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: There are too many.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: We cannot support them, and many cities are unable to support themselves.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Ever since the Profound Silence Iberia is not what it once was.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Then you need the support of others all the more.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: No one knows what happened to Iberia, and no one may know.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Because Iberia was once on the brink of total destruction?

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: Even now, Iberia cannot be destroyed.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are still here, and so are the Iberian people.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I believe that even if not a single city remained...

a.text: Kal'tsit looks at the three Abyssal Hunters. Of them, Skadi is walking toward some inhabitants exiting the buildings. Seems like she has something to say to them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Iberia's citizens won't give up so easily.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: High Inquisitor, please allow me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Pride and prejudice have destroyed the Ægir. This land must not repeat the mistakes of the deep sea folk.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If Iberia falls to the aftershock of this disaster, then there will no longer be anyone who knows the true face of the sea, and the horror of the threat it poses.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just like a certain hunt in the tundra roughly a century ago. It is the territory of mankind that we are guarding, not the honor and reputation of a nation, against the sea monsters, and against anything else.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Besides, if Iberia keeps lingering on with its last breath...

a.text: Kal'tsit looks into the High Inquisitor's eyes. His expression remains unchanged. He does not appear to be in denial, nor is he approving of her view.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In that case, Iberia will one day meet its fate.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As of now, you can still rebuild your homeland, rebuild Iberia.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: I don't believe that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: My objective isn't to get you to see things my way.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This question has to be answered, and a decision has to be made. It doesn't necessarily need to be answered by you, nor does it have to be now.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: We still must resolve the Sal Viento affair.

a.text: The High Inquisitor looks at the hunters.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: One of them will have to stay.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You two need to go back.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Kal'tsit, we will do as we discussed. I won't be there to lead them, so you will have to take my place.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You...?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What's this supposed to mean?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: High Inquisitor, perhaps I can take their place?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can serve as a proxy for them in your interrogations. I can straighten out the details of the events that transpired here, and you will get the information that you need.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can survive an Iberian prison.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: If you insist.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Lady Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Doctor...?

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: You want me to expel them from our territory?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: For now at the very least.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The three of you—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Go back to Rhodes Island. Misery will pick you up near the northeastern border. Don't take the waterways this time.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: The Inquisition will determine the route they will take.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As long as the destination remains unchanged, you may route them however you want.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: When will you come back? I can't wait for you too long.

steps.name: High Inquisitor
steps.text: That is not for her to decide.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Let's not jump to conclusions yet, little birdie of Iberia. A prison's walls are as paper to me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Gladiia, no.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: So you want me to watch him take you away?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Don't worry about me, Gladiia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now go, hunters. Surely a heart-to-heart with Specter must be on the agenda. Now that she's awake, she can give you the answers you've always wanted. Her own answers.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: And you have nothing to say to me? This is a rare opportunity for everyone, yourself included.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm afraid I don't have any suitable advice for a hunter like you.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Am I too hasty for your liking?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No, but you understand your own situation far better than I.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In any case, I don't know how much longer you can maintain your current state... Though I suppose that's the least of your worries.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: How do you know?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just a hunch. You are in a good mood, after all. I'm sure it matters to you very little whether you are awake or not, Specter. After all, the way things are now is not that bad for you.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You needn't tell me. Nothing has ever been completely optimal for us.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: And if I contemplate the future? That would be such a drag. My standards are much lower than yours. As long as things are decently sorted, they're good enough for me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I suppose so.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I am not one to preach the Church of the Deep's words, but that was me as well. There is no point in hating myself.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: If anyone wants to know the difference, then let them listen to me talk. I will settle for giving them a hard time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is this how you used to be?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Perhaps, Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Besides, I finally have some old friends here with me, not some landlubber that I wouldn't know how to talk to, even if I wanted to talk. You know, they haven't even seen seaweed before.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You could teach them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You still have a lot of new friends at that place you can now go back to.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In the future, your colleagues will need you. I will need all of you as well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We need you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Besides—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Well, don't come home too late!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This doctor is never late, Specter.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Let's go, hunters. We'll leave the rest to her. She can take it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Wait, Captain. I still have something to tell her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Lady Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Deploying without any approval again, Skadi.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At least you knew well enough to talk to Engineering and get them to prepare that case for you. They contacted me straight away.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're doing much better than before.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I didn't expect you to actually come help me...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I told you, I'm a woman of my word, and that goes no matter what it is you are up to.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now go home to Rhodes Island. Enjoy your vacation.
Kal'tsit glances at Skadi.
She doesn't say anything but starts smiling.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All of us have things that are simply beyond our abilities. Even Dr. {@nickname} struggles from time to time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Our technology is not yet able to cure your infection... And neither can you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But, Specter, not being able to eradicate it doesn't mean you can't defeat it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You can't exterminate shadows, but you can make them your friend.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Skadi...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There isn't much you can do about your dark fate... but you can learn to work alongside it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps only you can wrestle tooth and nail with it till the end of times.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Oh, it's you, singer! You are back!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh? Where's your sax... uh... saxophone?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No idea...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Oh, don't worry. I'm sure you left it somewhere around here. I'll help you look for it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Also, about your harp. You dropped it yesterday. I've been holding onto it for you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's yours now.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I can have it... Just like we promised? Does that mean you've found your friend? That's great news, singer. I'm so happy for you!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: But... you look really tired... You look more tired than you were last night. Are you hurt?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I... It's okay. I'm just a little dizzy.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Well, okay. I didn't see you, and I was so worried you ran into some kind of trouble.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Something really amazing happened just now. Did you see that? There was an explosion, then another. Like, bang bang bang, boooom! The mountain over that way kept shaking, and then it suddenly came crashing down!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I thought our house would come crashing down too.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Are you all okay?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: We're fine. The only problem is that all our food is still inside. It's already rotten. Erm, we'll probably go hungry for a while again.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's all thanks to the Inquisitor. She was the one who told us to leave the house and to stay away from the coast and the chapel up on the hill.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She helped you.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Yeah, she's such a nice person. She protected us the whole time.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Got a sore throat?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: *cough* *cough*— Y-You wretch! No matter, I will let you off the hook just this once. Tsk, you're a lucky one, Ægir. The High Inquisitor didn't take you away.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You've been waiting for me.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I knew you'd be back... I have something to tell you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Still haven't given up?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What...? Why are you in a fighting stance? I haven't even drawn my weapon!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: W-What I'm trying to say is... I'm sorry I was so harsh with you before.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I'm not the kind of person... who doesn't apologize when she's done wrong. I may be an Inquisitor, but when an Inquisitor makes a mistake, she needs to reflect on it all the more.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: When you first stepped into the town, I saw you right away. I could tell you were an Ægir, costume or no. You are different.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: At the time... I was angry, and my passions were inflamed. I thought I had finally found the answer. The evil outsiders, the culprit who brought this misfortune to us—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I thought that by dragging you out here and defeating you... I could right the wrongs and solve our problems. I thought it was that simple.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But I am no match for you, and what could defeating you change anyway?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The real threat that this city and all Iberia faces is not a single Ægir or two.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You've grown...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Much thanks to you...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I can't think the way I used to think anymore. What happened here has left me bewildered to the point that I'm not sure how I'd judge anything again.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I am an inquisitor. It is my duty to eradicate the threats that Iberia faces in order to uphold its order.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —You are a threat, but are you our enemy?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Then we have the people here. Should I protect them, or should they be eliminated?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: And what if I can't make sense of it? What, then, is my reason for taking up the sword? It will leave me directionless, stuck in the same spot, just like the people here.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Then—It was you and the locals who helped me see things clearly.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I can't save the inhabitants... It probably sounds strange, but once I realized this, I made the decision to protect them.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: At the very least, at that very moment and right now, I know what is right and what is wrong.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: As for you, you did the right thing. You protected this place... for the time being, at least. That is much more than I have ever done for these people.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You did the right thing too.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What I did was no different from what you did.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What do you mean, no different...? No matter, you are just as terrible at giving comfort as you are at disguises.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You wanted comfort from me?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What do you...? No, no thank you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Good. I don't have any for you either.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So, you found the answer you were looking for?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't need it anymore.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I've asked too many questions. I found my answer, and once I calmed down, I realized those answers meant nothing really. Just like you, I know which way I am headed now.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Oh? Seems we're both ready.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It's about time I get going, and I know it's time for you to go as well. You have gone free, so you must've come to some kind of agreement with the High Inquisitor.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Well... Goodbye.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: As long as we're still chasing the same goal, perhaps we will see each other again somewhere.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh? Did the Inquisitor leave? What a shame. I want her to see what I'm making.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What's this...?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's the seaweed alcohol you taught me to make! Uh, is this looking okay? Are the pieces too big still?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They are way too small.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh? Let me try again. It's okay. We don't have any food left, but we still have plenty of seaweed. If we run out, I'll get some more from Uncle Fireplace.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You will get better.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Once I'm finished... Uh... You'll be gone by the time I'm finished, right? You came here to tell me this, didn't you? You are leaving.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes, I'm leaving.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: (Subconsciously kneads the seaweed)

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Right, you're a wandering singer. You wander, only stopping once in a while.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Will you ever come back? I... I want to listen to you play your harp and sing some more. Grandma Petra and Drywall, they do too.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes, I will.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: My friends, too. We can come together.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: That sounds great!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's a promise, okay? Be sure to come back soon! I will be waiting for you here.

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Woodframe.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Uh, here! Singer, they need me for something. I gotta go.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Don't forget what you promised!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That can there...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The red shell.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Anita!

a.text: Just as she said she would, the girl stops in her tracks, turns around, and smiles at Skadi.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If next we meet on the outside, I'll still sing for you.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Okay! Looks like I gotta keep your harp in my box.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: See you, singer!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: See you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Dammit.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Dammit!
Gladiia caresses her face in the mirror.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Look at you. You still ended up an ugly bitch in the end.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You should've died in the deep sea. Is this what you wanted? You should've died with everyone else instead of going into hiding here. Constantly on edge, no matter what you do, even breathing, much less letting them hear your singing.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You have to shut yourself up in a landship's bathroom just to complain about your predicament, never again to ride the waves. All you can do is to wait until you fully transform into a beast.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Look, this is you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It's too soon... Too soon.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The ship... I need to find that ship.

a.text: A Seaborn tried to get an answer from Skadi... The monsters tried to pry the truth from their murderers.
Which also means that the hunters still have a chance, perhaps their one and only chance—

steps.text: Before the waves engulf the world and those monstrous colossi summon their bloodkin, we must smother the sea with silence. Its brood will know nothing of this.
We will exterminate them at their source.
This is our only chance. This will bring about a calamity... but Ægir will get its moment of reprieve.
I can't hear Ægir. Heh, just like the monsters waiting in vain for their revelations.
Nonetheless, we have a responsibility. The Abyssal Hunters must be the first to uncover Iberia's secrets.
—The last dreadnought of the Iberian fleet. Indomitable, yet disappearing without a trace in the span of a night.
Gladiia stops gazing at herself in the mirror.
This is my duty. I must defend Ægir.
By capturing that golden ship and taking hold of that key, the doors to the vault will fling wide open, and the volcano shall be unleashed.
